newsitem.title: CHINA: China launches sweeping agricultural survey.
newsitem.headline: China launches sweeping agricultural survey.

text.p: China launched on Wednesday an ambitious rural survey aimed at gathering more accurate data on its huge farming sector, the Xinhua news agency said.
More than six million interviewers will canvass some 800,000 villages to collect information on about 230 million households and 20 million rural enterprises, Xinhua said.

The effort would be aimed at determining the extent of cropland and the number of rural residents who have abandoned their farm tools for jobs in the cities, the agency quoted He Huanyan, an official with the National Agricultural Survey Office, as saying.
"China also hopes to know the size of rural households, the numbers of pigs, cows and chickens they raise, and the condition of their farm tools, implements and equipment in farming," He said.
The drive would take about one month to complete but authorities would need another two years to set up a national databank on the agricultural sector, the official said.
Some interviews were conducted in October in remote areas to avoid heavy winter snows anticipated during the survey period, He said.
The survey would be repeated every 10 years, the official said.
China must feed about one-fifth of the world's population on just seven percent of its arable land.
Beijing says a lack of accurate information about cropland has hampered its efforts to stop the misuse and erosion of farmland in the nation's drive towards food self sufficiency.
The government has also tried to check the flow of millions of rural labourers who flock to the cities every year in search of more lucrative jobs.
